headline: Google has launched Playground, an experimental tool that lets US adults build and share simple browser games by typing prompts.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the launch was on 7 Oct, before the window, and Google itself calls the tool an early experiment.
importance_line: People with no coding skills can try making games by describing them, but access is limited to US adults, creation depends on Google AI subscriptions, and Google calls it an early experiment.
summary: Mashable reports that Google launched Playground on 7 Oct 2026, a platform where people describe a game in a few prompts, refine it by chatting and then keep it private, share a link or publish it to a public gallery. It starts with US adults only, creation draws on weekly tokens tied to Google AI subscriptions, and Google calls it an "early experiment" that joins similar prompt-based tools from Roblox and Rosebud AI.
notes: Launch date 7 Oct 2026 (before the window); reported by Mashable on 8 Oct. Score 6 to 5.
